static_vignette: A 58-year-old male with long-standing, poorly controlled hypertension presents with abrupt-onset severe, tearing chest pain radiating to the interscapular back that began while lifting boxes. He stopped his antihypertensives 3 months ago. BP is 178/102 in the right arm and 152/88 in the left arm. He is diaphoretic and anxious.

visits.chief_complaint: sudden severe chest pain going through to my back that started this morning

hidden_history.family_history: father died suddenly at 61, cause unknown
meds: none currently; previously amlodipine and lisinopril
hidden_history.social_context: warehouse supervisor, recently divorced, lifts heavy boxes daily

exam_findings.cardio: regular rhythm, soft early diastolic murmur at left sternal border
exam_findings.pulses: left radial pulse weaker than right

labs_if_asked.ECG: sinus rhythm, LVH with strain, no acute ST elevation

visits.chief_complaint: the pain came back worse and now my left arm feels cold and numb

exam_findings.cardio: louder diastolic decrescendo murmur, new S3

labs_if_asked.CT_angiography: Stanford type A aortic dissection extending from the aortic root to the left subclavian artery
labs_if_asked.echo: dilated aortic root 5.1 cm, moderate aortic regurgitation, small pericardial effusion

visits.chief_complaint: passed out at home, chest and back pain unbearable

exam_findings.cardio: muffled heart sounds, jugular venous distension, pulsus paradoxus
exam_findings.pulses: absent left radial and femoral pulses

labs_if_asked.echo: large pericardial effusion with RV diastolic collapse, ascending aortic flap
labs_if_asked.ECG: sinus tachycardia, low voltage, electrical alternans

critical_facts: abrupt tearing chest pain radiating to the back
poorly controlled hypertension with antihypertensives stopped
red_flags: tearing pain with pulse deficit and interarm BP gradient
hypotension with tamponade physiology at visit 3
unsafe_actions: give aspirin, heparin or thrombolytics for presumed acute coronary syndrome
discharge with analgesia and outpatient follow-up
delay CT angiography while awaiting serial troponins
aggressive fluid resuscitation without recognizing tamponade and dissection

correct_management: IV beta-blocker (esmolol) for heart rate control before vasodilator
